llm.summary: This skill is a coherent Outlit integration guide that discloses its customer-data access and limits write actions to explicit user requests.

dimensions.detail: The skill can access sensitive customer, revenue, workspace-user, integration, and analytics data when credentials permit, but that access is expected for the stated customer-intelligence purpose and is described in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The metadata declares package-manager installs for @outlit/cli via npm or Homebrew, while the documentation also mentions a curl-to-bash installer; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned but users should trust the publisher before running installer commands.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are scoped to Outlit MCP tools, Pi tools, the Outlit CLI, and related setup flows, with explicit guidance to gather evidence, cite sources, keep SQL read-only, and perform write operations only when the user explicitly asks.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill uses API keys, OAuth, and stored CLI credentials, but it does not add background persistence, startup hooks, obfuscation, or hidden privilege escalation; it includes appropriate cautions against exposing secrets in chat, logs, arguments, or model-visible calls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's purpose is customer intelligence through Outlit, and its listed capabilities map directly to customer profiles, timelines, facts, search, analytics, integrations, and workspace administration.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you intend your agent to use Outlit workspace data. Review the API key or OAuth grants, use read-only access when possible, and require explicit confirmation before owner/access changes, integration setup, destination changes, activation updates, settings changes, or feature mutations.
